lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A crooked OPEN sign swings above the card shop door. Inside, a half-finished tournament bracket shares the counter with a pile of unopened packs.

lines.speaker: hana
lines.text: You must be the new challenger. Sorry about the mess. The bracket printer has opinions.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: I'll help with the bracket if you tell me where my name goes.

lines.speaker: hana
lines.text: Right under the newcomers. Thanks. Here's your schedule; the first event's on the back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Hana tries to straighten the sign through the glass. It swings the other way.

lines.speaker: hana
lines.text: You'll learn your way around. And if you don't, the shop's hard to miss.

choices.label: I want to test my best ideas.
choices.reply: Good. Try something strange in a practice game before you bring it to the cup.

choices.label: I want to understand this town first.
choices.reply: Then start with the café. Ask Alma what you should see first.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A noticeboard outside the community center is crowded with volunteers' names and a handwritten request for spare sleeves.

lines.speaker: shiori
lines.text: Someone's been erasing the same sign-up line for three days.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: The beginner's table?

lines.speaker: shiori
lines.text: Mm. They have two decks for six players. The owner of the shop lent them both.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A child approaches with a battered binder. Shiori pulls out a chair before returning to the board.

lines.speaker: shiori
lines.text: If you have a little time after your next match, they'd welcome another opponent.

choices.label: I can offer advice when I have time.
choices.reply: Thank you. Even one game would help. They keep running out of practice partners.

choices.label: I will cheer the volunteers on.
choices.reply: I'll tell them there's another friendly face in the crowd.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At the card shop, people crowd around a bracket penciled onto the back of a shipping carton. The Neighborhood Cup is tomorrow.

lines.speaker: reina
lines.text: Half those predictions are wrong already. They listed someone who's out of town.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You sound awfully sure of yourself.

lines.speaker: reina
lines.text: I'm sure of the matchup. The cards can still make a fool of me.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Reina flips a single test card onto the table, then leaves the rest of the deck face down.

lines.speaker: reina
lines.text: Got a minute? I want to see whether this opening's as bad as it looks.

choices.label: I will review my opening hands.
choices.reply: Good. Deal seven. We can find the ugly draws before tomorrow.

choices.label: I want to see who surprises everyone.
choices.reply: If you're watching, pay attention to the quiet games. That's where the strange decks hide.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A new qualifier bracket has been pinned above the community center's old results. Beside it sits a box of mismatched pens.

lines.speaker: akari
lines.text: Someone filled in the finalist before registration closed.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: That's a confident prediction.

lines.speaker: akari
lines.text: Or lazy bookkeeping. They're not remotely the same thing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She quietly crosses out the penciled name and offers the marker to the next player waiting in line.

lines.speaker: akari
lines.text: We should make sure everyone gets their place on the sheet first. After that, let them surprise us.

choices.label: I will prepare what I can.
choices.reply: Then bring the list you've actually tested. I'll be curious how it holds up.

choices.label: I will support the players who enter.
choices.reply: I'll save a seat by the last table. Those games are usually better than the predictions.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Championship posters have gone up along the waterfront. In the shop window, a sun-faded schedule from the first week still hangs beneath the new one.

lines.speaker: hana
lines.text: Look at that. I never took the old schedule down.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You could leave it there.

lines.speaker: hana
lines.text: It has someone's tea stain on it. And the wrong start time for the second cup.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She smooths one corner against the glass, careful not to tear the paper.

lines.speaker: hana
lines.text: After the final, I'm making everybody bring a deck back here. Win or lose.

choices.label: One more practice session sounds right.
choices.reply: All right, but eat something before the match. You keep forgetting.

choices.label: I want to thank the people who helped.
choices.reply: You should. I still have the signup sheet from the first week.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The last tournament notices come down. The shop keeps one page from the final results book on the counter.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The season record reads: {{seasonRecord}}. {{championshipRecord}}

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A second page holds the names from your time around town. {{friendshipRecord}}

lines.speaker: shiori
lines.text: The café's still open, if you want to sit for a while.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Feels strange without another round on the schedule.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Shiori closes the results book and leaves it beside the spare decks.

lines.speaker: shiori
lines.text: Then perhaps next time we can play without looking at the clock.

choices.label: I am ready for whatever comes next.
choices.reply: I'll put the kettle on. Someone will arrive with a deck before the water boils.

choices.label: I want a moment to remember it.
choices.reply: There's no rush. The chairs aren't going anywhere.
